records.family: Linux process/resource hierarchy and aggregate overcommit
records.version_context: Version 7.1 doc plus mutable latest alias separately fetched.
records.locator: Process organization; controller enablement/delegation; limits; cpu.weight/max; memory.max; pids.max; io.max; cgroup.kill.
records.observations: Fork inherits membership. Controllers need availability/enabling and suitable rights. Memory defaults unlimited and may temporarily exceed max; CPU weights apply to eligible scheduler classes. Child limits may overcommit parent capacity. io.max throttles device throughput. Non-root, non-threaded cgroup.kill covers the subtree and concurrent forks.
records.applicability_limits: Resource cgroups are not file-access authority, app admission order, guaranteed interactive latency, or storage-capacity quotas. Prevent migration out before relying on tree teardown.

records.family: Windows job membership, termination, memory and CPU
records.version_context: Living Win32 docs; nested jobs and CPU rate control require Windows 8/Server 2012+.
records.locator: Create/assign/terminate job; breakaway; LimitFlags and extended structures; CPU interval/DFSS.
records.observations: CreateProcess children usually join; breakaway and WMI creation are exceptions. Memory flags constrain committed virtual memory. Job time is user-mode execution, not wall time. CPU hard caps pause members after interval consumption.
records.applicability_limits: Verify membership and explicit flags. Job Objects do not set file ACLs. CPU rate controls have Remote Desktop DFSS restrictions.
